text:
Situation: Carboplatin has been on the FDA drug shortage list since 2023-04-28 and remains current as of 2026-10-21, a period of 42 months. Corvale Lakeside holds critically low stock (1.5–2.5 days on hand). Corvale East holds two products (Teva NDC 00703423901 from PHARMACHEMIE BV and Apotex NDC 60505628201 from Teyro Labs Private Limited) with 15–20 days on hand. Corvale General holds three listings with approximately 9 days on hand each.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the carboplatin shortage on 2023-04-28. The Accord Healthcare product on the shortage list uses Intas Pharmaceuticals Limited as a registered manufacturing plant. FDA inspection 1191818 of Intas Pharmaceuticals Limited ended 2022-12-02 and was classified OAI, with the classification letter dated 2023-04-05, 23 days before the shortage posting. FDA subsequently issued import alert 66-40 listing Intas Pharmaceuticals Limited on 2023-06-01 and a Warning Letter on 2023-07-28.

Our position: We have sufficient supply at Corvale East to support internal transfers without dropping below two weeks on hand. Approved therapeutic alternatives exist for the same molecule from Apotex Corp. and Teva Parenteral Medicines, Inc.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 26 units from Corvale East to Corvale Lakeside — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
2. Transfer 2 units from Corvale East to Corvale General — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
3. Use same product, alternate manufacturer: CARBOplatin 10 mg/mL from Apotex Corp. (substitute NDC) — approved by pharmacist per Alex Morgan, PharmD on 2026-05-16.
4. Use same molecule, alternate concentration or vial size: CARBOplatin 10 mg/mL from Teva Parenteral Medicines, Inc. (recalculate dose and volume) — approved by pharmacist per Casey Nguyen, MD on 2026-01-18.

Not recommended: Purchasing additional Accord Healthcare carboplatin manufactured by Intas Pharmaceuticals Limited while the import alert and Warning Letter remain in effect.
